title: Algorithmic Bias, Generalist Models, and Clinical Medicine

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical analysis and literature review of biases in clinical models, including disparities in dermatological datasets by skin tone, proxy variables like healthcare costs misrepresenting healthcare needs, and the disproportionate use of negative descriptors for Black patients in electronic health records.

Conceptual evaluation using examples from prior literature to demonstrate stereotype associations (e.g., language models associating Muslims with violence) and semantic haze regarding minority religious practices (e.g., Islamic marriage customs).

Theoretical examination of perspectival biases in language model outputs (e.g., heteronormative definitions of family) and the adverse effects of inappropriate data filtration on LGBTQ+ terminology and discourse.

Literature-based analysis of how demographic underrepresentation in clinical training data leads to suboptimal predictive performance, utilizing stroke risk assessment in older women as an illustrative example.
Theoretical discussion of 'semantic haze' caused by the disproportionate representation of Western/US discourse compared to Global South countries in internet text pre-training datasets.
Conceptual evaluation of how conversational clinical interfaces might alienate nomadic communities (e.g., the Irish Traveller community) due to implicit cultural assumptions in language models.
Theoretical discussion regarding the inequitable availability of health information and safety screening tools across different languages (e.g., English vs. Spanish).
